summary: A person or entity marker. Content is chosen by precedence — image, then initials, then icon — not by a type prop.
useWhen: identifying who owns, authored or is assigned to something
a table cell, menu row or header needs a compact identity marker beside a name

useInstead.when: the thing being marked is a status, count or category rather than a person
you only need a decorative graphic with no identity behind it

mini.use: 24px — inline beside body text, dense table rows

square.use: organisations, projects, workspaces and other non-human entities

neutral.use: no state, or a state this system has no colour for

primary.use: attention rather than health — a request, an invite, a mention

warning.use: away, idle, needs attention but is not broken

information.use: a neutral fact about the person — a role or a badge, not a state

icon.note: the last fallback — rendered only when there is neither `src` nor `initials`

topIndicatorIcon.note: replaces the top indicator's default check glyph. The bottom indicator takes no glyph — Figma draws it bare, and at Mini it is 8px, which nothing legible fits inside.

guarantees: `alt` falls back to `initials`, so the avatar is never announced as an unlabelled image
a `src` that fails to load falls through to initials, then icon — never the browser's broken-image glyph

indicator labels are announced wherever they land: folded into the avatar's own `aria-label` when there is no image (the root is `role="img"` and therefore a leaf), and carried as hidden text inside each indicator when there is
requires: `alt` describing the person, not the picture — "Ada Lovelace", not "profile photo"

`topIndicatorLabel` / `bottomIndicatorLabel` on any indicator that carries meaning. An indicator with no label is decorative, which is the right answer only when the same fact is already stated in text beside it.

antiPatterns.why: a 404 leaves the fallback empty; initials are what make the failure invisible

antiPatterns.do: put the Avatar inside a Button or Link
antiPatterns.why: Avatar renders a <span> with no role and takes no focus

antiPatterns.dont: using an indicator's colour as the only carrier of a status
antiPatterns.do: pass `topIndicatorLabel` / `bottomIndicatorLabel`, or state the status in text nearby
antiPatterns.why: WCAG 1.4.1. A green dot and a red dot are the same dot to a screen reader, and to a good share of sighted users too

antiPatterns.dont: reaching for `ring` to mean selected or focused
antiPatterns.why: it is a static brand ring from the design, not a focus indicator. Focus belongs on whatever interactive element wraps the avatar, and that element draws its own
